rationale:
structural: The only structural obligation is the prescribed signature: `impl<'d, D: Domain> ValidationContext<'d, D> { pub fn read(&self, node: &NodeId<D>) -> Result<D::NodeContent, D::Error>; }`. The root `crates/trust-but-verify/src/procedure.rs#impl[ValidationContext<'d, D>]#2/fn[read]` declares exactly that: a method on the generic impl, taking `&self` and `&NodeId<D>`, and returning `Result<D::NodeContent, D::Error>`. It is marked {impl}. An alternative with a different signature, such as taking `NodeId` by value or returning a different error type, would break the stated declaration. So this obligation needs evidence, and the root supplies it.

The other clauses state behavior only: "Read a graph node and record the fingerprint of the returned contents". The text names no library, algorithm or interface through which recording must happen. An implementation that records inline would give the same behavior, so how the recording is factored is discretionary. The `read_node.inputs` text is cited context. It describes when the fingerprint is recorded and that a failed read records nothing. Those are behavioral, and tests cover them.

The code does implement the behavior. `read` calls `read_snapshot`. `read_snapshot` calls `prepare_read(node)?`, then `record_read(*node, snapshot.fingerprint.clone())`, then returns the snapshot. `read` returns `.content`. A failed `prepare_read` returns early through `?`, so nothing is recorded. `record_read` pushes `Dependency::Node(node, fingerprint)` onto the observations. These helpers are reached from the marked root, so they need no separate reference.

behavioral: The subject requires `ValidationContext::read` to return the node's contents. On success it must record the node identity and the fingerprint of the returned contents. A failed read must record no observation. The evidence goes stale when a later read of the same node has a different fingerprint. I did not read the implementation. The checks below come from the supplied tests.

- **Success records identity and fingerprint.** `snapshots_record_exact_reads_and_retain_distinct_versions` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs` starts with empty dependencies. It reads node 1 containing "before" and asserts the content. It then asserts `dependencies()` equals `[Dependency::Node(intern_node(1), fp("before"))]`.
- **Fingerprint follows the returned contents.** The same test changes the node to "after" and reads again. It asserts the content is "after" and that the dependencies are the two entries for before and after. The earlier snapshot `earlier` stays unchanged.
- **Failed read records nothing.** The same test reads missing node 2 and asserts an error. The dependencies afterwards are still the two node-1 entries. `direct_reads_return_complete_unicode_contents_and_snapshots` asserts the error is "missing" and that a fresh context has empty `dependencies()` after the failed read.
- **Staleness.** After `finish`, `record.dependencies` holds the before and after entries. The test asserts `!record.is_current(...)` because node 1's content now differs from one recorded fingerprint. The second test makes the same assertion after replacing the content.
- **Content shapes.** `direct_reads_return_complete_unicode_contents_and_snapshots` covers empty and large multi-byte Unicode strings. It asserts the returned `contents.format()` equals the original and that the recorded fingerprint equals `fp(original)`. It also asserts the returned contents are unaffected by a later change to the graph.

The delivery paragraph in `read_node.inputs` describes how an agent harness records fingerprints. It does not add an obligation to this Rust `read`. The text says that for a Rust caller the fingerprint is recorded when `read` returns the contents, and the tests check that. `public_exports_match_the_appendix` only checks the public export inventory and is not needed for the behavior. I found no gap.

text: :::{req} ValidationContext.read
Read a graph node and record the fingerprint of the returned contents under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.inputs`.
```rust,ignore
impl<'d, D: Domain> ValidationContext<'d, D> {
pub fn read(&self, node: &NodeId<D>) -> Result<D::NodeContent, D::Error>;
:::{req} read_node.inputs
A successful `ValidationContext::read` records the node's identity and the
fingerprint of the returned contents, under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs`. A failed read records no
successful observation. The evidence becomes stale when a later read of that
node has a different fingerprint; a failure to resolve it is reported by
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records`.
For a Rust caller, the SDK records the fingerprint when `read` returns the
contents. For an agent, the harness puts a tool result in the next request to
the model and records the fingerprint once the provider responds successfully.
That successful exchange is *delivery*. For example, suppose the tool reads a
function that returns `3`, and someone changes it to return `4` before the
provider responds. The model saw the version that returns `3`, so the SDK
records the fingerprint it computed from that version. Reading the function
again at this point would record a fingerprint for code the model never saw.
